def: A job that is available because nobody is doing it yet or the previous holder has left.

formal.ex: A [[vacancy]] has arisen in the Finance Department following an internal promotion.
formal.ex_us: A [[vacant position]] has arisen in the Finance Department following an internal promotion.

everyday.ex: We've got a [[vacancy]] in the payroll team - do you know anyone who might be interested?
everyday.ex_us: We've got an [[opening]] on the payroll team - do you know anyone who might be interested?

collocations: to have a vacancy for an analyst
a vacancy in the sales team
note_fr: Ne dites pas « a free post » ni « an open post ». « Vacancy » est surtout britannique ; un Américain dira « an opening » ou « an open position » (et « vacancy » lui évoquera plutôt une chambre d'hôtel libre). Attention : « vacation » = vacances.

def: A written statement of the purpose, main tasks and responsibilities of a job.

formal.ex: The duties of the post are set out in the attached [[job description]], which may be reviewed from time to time.

everyday.ex: Could you update the [[job description]] before we go out to market?

informal.ex: Send me the [[JD]] and I'll have a look tonight.

collocations: to draw up a job description
to fall outside one's job description
note_fr: Pas de « job sheet » ni de « post file ». La « job description » décrit le poste ; le profil du candidat idéal figure dans la « person specification » (UK) ou sous « qualifications / requirements » (US). L'abréviation « JD » est courante à l'oral et dans les e-mails internes.

def: The list of skills, experience and qualifications that the ideal candidate for a job should have.

formal.ex: Candidates will be assessed solely against the criteria listed in the [[person specification]].
formal.ex_us: Candidates will be assessed solely against the criteria listed in the [[job requirements]].

everyday.ex: She ticks almost every box on the [[person spec]].
everyday.ex_us: She checks almost every box on the [[requirements]].

note_fr: « Profile » seul désigne plutôt le profil d'un candidat donné (« a strong profile »). Au Royaume-Uni, on distingue les critères « essential » et « desirable » ; aux États-Unis, les « required » et « preferred qualifications ». « Wanted profile » est un calque à éviter.

fr: manager recruteur (le responsable opérationnel qui recrute pour son équipe)
def: The manager who has the vacancy in his or her team and makes the final decision on whom to appoint.

formal.ex: The [[recruiting manager]] is responsible for ensuring that all interview notes are returned to Human Resources.
formal.ex_us: The [[hiring manager]] is responsible for ensuring that all interview notes are returned to Human Resources.

everyday.ex: The [[hiring manager]] wants to see three candidates before the end of the month.

collocations: to get the hiring manager's sign-off
to take the brief from the hiring manager
note_fr: Le « hiring manager » n'est pas le recruteur : c'est le futur supérieur hiérarchique, celui qui a le besoin. Le recruteur interne est « the recruiter » ou « the talent acquisition partner ». « Operational manager » ne rend pas cette idée.

fr: demande d'ouverture de poste (validation interne avant de recruter)
def: The internal request, approved by management and finance, that authorises a team to recruit for a post.

formal.ex: No vacancy may be advertised until the [[recruitment authorisation request]] has been approved by the Finance Director.
formal.ex_us: No vacancy may be advertised until the [[job requisition]] has been approved by the Finance Director.

everyday.ex: We can't brief the agency yet - we still haven't got [[approval to recruit]].
everyday.ex_us: We can't brief the agency yet - we still don't have an [[approved requisition]].

informal.ex: Has the [[sign-off]] come through for the analyst role?
informal.ex_us: Has the [[req]] come through for the analyst role?

note_fr: « Requisition » n'a rien de militaire ici : c'est le terme américain (abrégé « req ») pour la demande de recrutement validée. Au Royaume-Uni, on parle plus volontiers de « approval to recruit » ou de « headcount approval ». « Headcount » = l'effectif budgété.

fr: remplacement d'un salarié parti (par opposition à une création de poste)
def: A person recruited to take over a post left empty by someone who has resigned, moved or gone on long leave.

formal.ex: This is a [[replacement appointment]] and therefore does not increase the approved headcount.
formal.ex_us: This is a [[replacement hire]] and therefore does not increase the approved headcount.

everyday.ex: It's not a new role, it's a [[backfill]] for Tom, who moved to the Lyon office.

collocations: to cover for someone on leave
note_fr: « To backfill a role » = pourvoir un poste laissé vacant ; le mot, d'origine américaine, est désormais courant dans les groupes internationaux. Une création de poste se dit « a new role » ou « a newly created position », jamais « a post creation ».

def: To find and appoint someone for a job that is available.

formal.ex: The Company reserves the right [[to fill a vacancy]] before the advertised closing date.
formal.ex_us: The Company reserves the right [[to fill a position]] before the advertised closing date.

everyday.ex: It took us four months [[to fill the role]].

collocations: to struggle to fill a role
note_fr: Le verbe est « to fill », jamais « to provide a post » ni « to fulfil a position » (« to fulfil » = remplir une obligation, une condition). Tournure très utile pour répondre à un candidat : « I'm afraid the position has now been filled. »

def: A public notice describing a job that is available and inviting people to apply.

formal.ex: The [[job advertisement]] must state the type of contract and the place of work.
formal.ex_us: The [[job posting]] must state the type of contract and the place of work.

everyday.ex: I saw your [[job advert]] on LinkedIn last week.
everyday.ex_us: I saw your [[job posting]] on LinkedIn last week.

informal.ex: The [[job ad]] doesn't even mention the salary.

collocations: to respond to a job advert
note_fr: Faux ami majeur : « a job offer » est la proposition d'embauche faite à un candidat précis, pas l'annonce. « Announcement » ne convient pas non plus. Prononciation : « adVERtisement » /ədˈvɜːtɪsmənt/ au Royaume-Uni, « ADvertisement » /ˈædvərtaɪzmənt/ aux États-Unis.

fr: publier une annonce / diffuser une offre
def: To make a job opening public so that people can apply for it.

formal.ex: All vacancies shall be [[advertised]] internally for at least one week before being opened to external candidates.
formal.ex_us: All positions shall be [[posted]] internally for at least one week before being opened to external candidates.

everyday.ex: We [[put the advert out]] on Monday and we've already had sixty applications.
everyday.ex_us: We [[posted the job]] on Monday and we've already had sixty applications.

collocations: to post a job on LinkedIn
note_fr: « To publish an announce » est un double calque. On dit « to advertise a job / a role » (UK) ou « to post a job » (US, et partout pour une mise en ligne). « To go out to market » = lancer la recherche en externe.

def: A website where employers publish vacancies and jobseekers look for work.

formal.ex: Vacancies are published on the Company's careers page and on at least one [[online recruitment platform]].

everyday.ex: Most of our applicants come through one [[job board]], to be honest.

collocations: to post a vacancy on a job board
note_fr: « Job site » se comprend, mais « job board » est le terme du métier. La page « Recrutement » du site de l'entreprise s'appelle « the careers page » (UK) ou « the careers site » (US), pas « the recruitment page ».

def: The last day on which applications for a job will be accepted.

formal.ex: The [[closing date for applications]] is Friday 14 March; late applications will not be considered.
formal.ex_us: The [[application deadline]] is Friday, March 14; late applications will not be considered.

everyday.ex: When's the [[closing date]] for the HR Adviser role?
everyday.ex_us: When's the [[deadline]] for the HR Advisor role?

collocations: to apply before the closing date
note_fr: « Limit date » et « dead line » (en deux mots) sont fautifs. « Closing date » est l'usage britannique des annonces ; « deadline » est compris partout. Notez aussi la tournure « Applications close on... ».

def: A phrase used in job adverts to say that the pay offered will depend on what the successful candidate brings.

formal.ex: Permanent, full-time position; [[salary dependent on experience]].
formal.ex_us: Permanent, full-time position; [[salary commensurate with experience]].

everyday.ex: We're offering somewhere between 45 and 52, [[depending on experience]].

informal.ex: The advert just says 'competitive salary, [[DOE]]', which tells you nothing.

note_fr: Jamais « salary according to profile ». « Commensurate with » (à la mesure de) est soutenu et typiquement américain. La transparence salariale progresse : plusieurs États américains imposent d'indiquer une fourchette dans l'annonce, et une directive européenne va dans le même sens ; vérifiez la règle applicable avant de publier.

def: The work of actively looking for and identifying potential candidates, rather than waiting for applications.

formal.ex: [[Candidate sourcing]] for senior roles is carried out by the in-house Talent Acquisition team.

everyday.ex: We [[source most of our candidates]] through LinkedIn and referrals.

note_fr: Le verbe « to source » est transitif : « to source candidates », sans préposition. « Research of candidates » est un calque : « research » = la recherche scientifique ; pour la recherche de candidats, on dit « search » ou « sourcing ».

def: A group of people an employer has identified as potential candidates for future vacancies.

formal.ex: With your consent, we will retain your details in our [[talent pool]] and may contact you about future vacancies.

everyday.ex: She came second this time, so let's keep her in the [[talent pool]].
everyday.ex_us: She came in second this time, so let's keep her in the [[talent pipeline]].

collocations: to tap into a talent pool
to keep someone's CV on file
note_fr: Ni « fishpond » ni « nursery » : l'image anglaise est celle du bassin (« pool ») ou du pipeline. « We'll keep your CV on file » est la formule consacrée ; conserver un CV suppose toutefois d'en informer le candidat, et pour une durée limitée.

def: The reputation and image a company has as a place to work, among its staff and potential recruits.

formal.ex: A consistent candidate experience is central to the Group's [[employer brand]].

everyday.ex: Leaving candidates without an answer does real damage to our [[reputation as an employer]].

note_fr: « Employer brand » désigne l'image elle-même, « employer branding » le travail mené pour la construire. « Employer mark » est un calque. Retenez aussi « an employer of choice » (un employeur de référence) et « employee value proposition » (EVP), la promesse faite aux salariés.

def: The recommendation of a candidate for a vacancy by someone who already works for the company.

formal.ex: A bonus is payable for any [[employee referral]] that results in an appointment, once the new recruit has completed six months' service.

everyday.ex: One of our developers [[referred her]], and she turned out to be excellent.

collocations: to recommend someone for a role
note_fr: « Cooptation » existe en anglais mais relève de la science politique : personne ne le comprendra en RH. Dites « referral » ; le programme est un « referral scheme » (UK) ou « referral program » (US), la prime un « referral bonus ».

def: A company that finds candidates for employers in exchange for a fee.

formal.ex: The Company has engaged a [[recruitment consultancy]] to assist with the appointment.
formal.ex_us: The Company has engaged a [[recruiting firm]] to assist with the appointment.

everyday.ex: We'll have to go through a [[recruitment agency]] for this one - we don't have the network.
everyday.ex_us: We'll have to go through a [[recruiting agency]] for this one - we don't have the network.

note_fr: « Cabinet » est un faux ami (meuble, ou conseil des ministres) : on dit « agency », « firm » ou « consultancy ». Le consultant du cabinet est « a recruitment consultant » (UK) ou « a recruiter » (US). Au Royaume-Uni, on « instruct » une agence ; aux États-Unis, on « engage » ou « retain » un cabinet.

def: A recruiter who approaches people directly, usually for senior jobs, rather than advertising.

formal.ex: The Board has appointed an [[executive search consultant]] to identify candidates for the role of Chief Financial Officer.

everyday.ex: A [[headhunter]] rang me last week about a job in Geneva.
everyday.ex_us: A [[headhunter]] called me last week about a job in Geneva.

collocations: to be approached by a headhunter
note_fr: « Headhunter » est courant mais familier : dans un document, écrivez « executive search firm / consultant ». Le passif est très utile : « She was headhunted by a competitor » = elle a été approchée directement par un concurrent.

fr: mandat de recherche exclusif (honoraires dus quel que soit le résultat)
def: A recruitment assignment in which the employer pays the search firm part of its fee in advance, whether or not anyone is hired.

formal.ex: The appointment will be conducted as a [[retained search assignment]], the fee being payable in three instalments.
formal.ex_us: The appointment will be conducted as a [[retained search assignment]], the fee being payable in three installments.

everyday.ex: For a role this senior, I'd go for a [[retained search]] rather than three agencies racing each other.

note_fr: L'opposition à connaître : « retained » (acompte, exclusivité) contre « contingency » (honoraires dus seulement en cas d'embauche ; au Royaume-Uni : « no placement, no fee »). « A retainer » est la provision versée d'avance, pas une retenue sur salaire.

def: To persuade someone who works for another company, often a competitor, to come and work for you.

formal.ex: The agency undertakes not [[to solicit the employees of]] the Client for twelve months after the end of the assignment.

everyday.ex: They [[poached]] two of our best engineers last year.

informal.ex: A start-up [[lured him away]] with share options.
informal.ex_us: A startup [[lured him away]] with stock options.

collocations: to poach staff from a competitor
note_fr: « To debauch » signifie dépraver, corrompre moralement : contresens garanti. « To poach » (littéralement braconner) est le mot juste, un peu imagé mais admis en réunion. Attention : les accords de non-débauchage entre concurrents (« no-poach agreements ») peuvent poser un problème de droit de la concurrence.

fr: candidat passif (en poste, pas en recherche active)
def: Someone who is not looking for a new job but might be open to the right opportunity.

formal.ex: The search firm will approach [[passive candidates]] identified through market mapping.

everyday.ex: The best person for this is probably [[someone who isn't actively looking]].

note_fr: L'expression clé côté candidat : « I'm not actively looking, but I'm open to the right opportunity. » Évitez « in post candidate » ; « to be in post » existe au Royaume-Uni mais signifie seulement « occuper le poste ».

fr: recruter en interne / privilégier la promotion interne
def: To fill a vacancy with someone who already works for the organisation.

formal.uk: to fill a vacancy by internal appointment
formal.us: to fill a position by internal appointment
formal.ex: Wherever possible, the Company will seek [[to fill vacancies by internal appointment]].
formal.ex_us: Wherever possible, the Company will seek [[to fill positions by internal appointment]].

everyday.ex: I'd rather [[recruit internally]] if we can - it's quicker and it's good for morale.
everyday.ex_us: I'd rather [[hire internally]] if we can - it's quicker and it's good for morale.

note_fr: « Internal mobility » existe, mais la tournure idiomatique est « to promote from within ». Un candidat interne est « an internal candidate » ou « an internal applicant », jamais « an intern » : « an intern » est un stagiaire.

fr: recrutement de jeunes diplômés / relations écoles
def: The organised hiring of students and recent graduates, usually through universities and yearly intakes.

formal.ex: The annual [[graduate recruitment]] campaign opens in September.
formal.ex_us: The annual [[campus recruiting]] campaign opens in September.

everyday.ex: We're taking on twelve people in [[the graduate intake]] this year.
everyday.ex_us: We're taking on twelve people in [[the new grad class]] this year.

note_fr: « Graduate » désigne au Royaume-Uni un diplômé de l'université ; aux États-Unis, « college graduate » ou « new grad ». « Graduate scheme » (UK) = programme jeunes diplômés ; « the milk round » (UK, familier) = la tournée annuelle des campus. Un salon de l'emploi : « careers fair » (UK), « job fair / career fair » (US).

def: Jobs for which employers struggle to find enough suitably skilled candidates.

formal.ex: Simplified work permit procedures may apply to [[shortage occupations]] listed by the authorities.

everyday.ex: Welders and nurses are our [[hard-to-fill roles]] - we never get enough applicants.
everyday.ex_us: Welders and nurses are our [[hard-to-fill positions]] - we never get enough applicants.

note_fr: « Jobs in tension » ne veut rien dire. On parle de « skills shortage » (pénurie de compétences), de « shortage occupations » (terme administratif) ou d'un « tight labour market » (US : « labor »). En France, une liste officielle de métiers en tension facilite la délivrance de certaines autorisations de travail.

def: The government body that registers jobseekers, pays unemployment benefit and helps employers fill vacancies.

formal.ex: The vacancy has also been registered with France Travail, [[the public employment service]].

everyday.ex: We've listed the job with France Travail - it's the French equivalent of [[the job centre]].
everyday.ex_us: We've listed the job with France Travail - it's the French equivalent of [[the unemployment office]].

collocations: to list a vacancy with the public employment service
note_fr: Gardez le nom français et glosez-le. L'équivalent britannique est « Jobcentre Plus » ; aux États-Unis, ce rôle est réparti entre les agences des États (« state workforce agency », « American Job Center »). « Pole employment » n'existe pas. Un demandeur d'emploi : « a jobseeker ».

explain.written: France Travail (formerly Pôle emploi) is the French public employment service, which registers jobseekers, pays unemployment benefits and assists employers with recruitment.
explain.spoken: France Travail is the French job centre - it's where people sign on when they're out of work, and employers can list vacancies there for free.

def: A person who is being considered for a job.

formal.ex: Each [[applicant]] will be informed in writing of the outcome of the selection process.

everyday.ex: We've got one really strong [[candidate]] and two possibles.

note_fr: Nuance : « applicant » = toute personne ayant déposé une candidature ; « candidate » = plutôt celle qui est effectivement dans le processus. « Postulant » n'existe pas dans ce sens (c'est un terme religieux). Prononciation : /ˈkændɪdət/ (UK), souvent /ˈkændɪdeɪt/ (US).

def: To ask formally to be considered for a job, usually by sending a CV.

formal.ex: Candidates are invited [[to submit an application]] via the Company's careers page.

everyday.ex: I [[applied for]] the HR Manager role last week and haven't heard anything.

informal.ex: Are you going [[to go for]] the team leader job?

note_fr: Deux prépositions à ne pas confondre : « to apply FOR a job » (un poste) mais « to apply TO a company » (une entreprise). « To postulate » = poser un postulat ; « to candidate » n'existe pas.

def: A formal request to be considered for a job, with the documents that support it.

formal.ex: Your [[application]] will be treated in the strictest confidence.

everyday.ex: Thanks for your [[application]] - we'll be in touch by the end of next week.

collocations: to acknowledge receipt of an application
note_fr: « Candidature » est très rare en anglais professionnel : dites « application ». « Candidacy » existe surtout aux États-Unis, dans un registre soutenu ou politique. Accusé de réception d'une candidature : « an acknowledgement ».

def: A short written summary of a person's education, career and skills, sent when applying for a job.

formal.ex: Applications should include a full [[curriculum vitae]] and the names of two referees.
formal.ex_us: Applications should include a full [[résumé]] and the names of two references.

everyday.ex: Can you send me your [[CV]] by Friday?
everyday.ex_us: Can you send me your [[résumé]] by Friday?

collocations: to tailor one's CV to the role
to look good on a CV
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, « CV » ; aux États-Unis, « résumé » (souvent écrit « resume »), court, d'une à deux pages - « CV » y désigne le dossier détaillé des universitaires et des médecins. Dans les deux pays, ni photo, ni âge, ni situation de famille. Et « a resume » n'est jamais un résumé de texte (« a summary »).

def: A letter sent with a CV, explaining why the person is applying and why they suit the job.

formal.ex: Please send your CV and a [[covering letter]] to the address below.
formal.ex_us: Please send your résumé and a [[cover letter]] to the address below.

everyday.ex: Her [[covering letter]] was far better than her CV, actually.
everyday.ex_us: Her [[cover letter]] was far better than her résumé, actually.

note_fr: « Motivation letter » est un calque, compris seulement dans les milieux européens. « Covering letter » est l'usage britannique traditionnel, « cover letter » l'usage américain, de plus en plus répandu partout. Elle tient en une page et s'ouvre sur le poste visé, pas sur une formule de politesse.

def: An application sent to a company that has not advertised any vacancy.

formal.ex: The Company is unable to reply individually to every [[speculative application]] it receives.
formal.ex_us: The Company is unable to reply individually to every [[unsolicited application]] it receives.

everyday.uk: to send one's CV on spec
everyday.ex: I just [[sent my CV on spec]] and they called me the next day.
everyday.ex_us: I just [[sent my résumé cold]] and they called me the next day.

collocations: to write in on the off-chance
note_fr: « Spontaneous application » est le calque classique : en anglais, « spontaneous » évoque l'impulsivité, pas l'initiative. « On spec » (UK, familier) = à tout hasard. Aux États-Unis, on dit « unsolicited » ou « cold » (comme dans « cold call »).

fr: je vous adresse ma candidature au poste de...

term.uk: I am writing to apply for the position of...
term.us: I am writing to apply for the position of...

ipa.uk: /aɪ əm ˈraɪtɪŋ tu əˈplaɪ fə ðə pəˈzɪʃ(ə)n əv/
ipa.us: /aɪ əm ˈraɪtɪŋ tu əˈplaɪ fər ðə pəˈzɪʃ(ə)n əv/

def: The standard opening sentence of a letter or email of application.

formal.uk: I am writing to apply for the position of
formal.us: I am writing to apply for the position of
formal.ex: [[I am writing to apply for the position of]] Payroll Manager, as advertised on your website.

everyday.ex: [[I'd like to apply for]] the HR Adviser role you posted last week.
everyday.ex_us: [[I'd like to apply for]] the HR Advisor role you posted last week.

note_fr: Allez droit au but : pas de « I allow myself to send you my application » (calque de « je me permets ») ni de « I have the honour to ». La première phrase nomme le poste et la source de l'annonce ; la deuxième dit pourquoi vous.

term.uk: I look forward to hearing from you
term.us: I look forward to hearing from you

ipa.uk: /aɪ lʊk ˈfɔːwəd tə ˈhɪərɪŋ frəm juː/
ipa.us: /aɪ lʊk ˈfɔːrwərd tə ˈhɪrɪŋ frəm juː/

def: The usual polite closing sentence of a letter or email when a reply is expected.

formal.uk: I look forward to hearing from you
formal.us: I look forward to hearing from you
formal.ex: I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application further and [[I look forward to hearing from you]].

everyday.uk: Looking forward to hearing from you
everyday.us: Looking forward to hearing from you
everyday.ex: Thanks again for your time on Tuesday. [[Looking forward to hearing from you]].

collocations: I look forward to meeting you
I look forward to your reply
I would welcome the opportunity to discuss
note_fr: Piège grammatical : « to » est ici une préposition, donc suivi de -ing : « to hearing », jamais « to hear ». « In the waiting of your answer » et « Waiting for your answer » sont à proscrire (le second sonne comme un reproche).

def: The jobs a person has done and the knowledge and skills gained from them.

formal.ex: Applicants must have at least five years' [[professional experience]] in a comparable role.

everyday.ex: She's got a lot of [[experience]] in retail, but none in logistics.
everyday.ex_us: She has a lot of [[experience]] in retail, but none in logistics.

note_fr: « Experience » au sens de vécu professionnel est indénombrable : « she has experience », jamais « an experience » ni « experiences ». Notez l'apostrophe de « five years' experience ». Au Royaume-Uni, « work experience » désigne aussi le stage d'observation des lycéens.

def: The degrees, diplomas and certificates that show a person has completed a course of study or training.

formal.ex: The offer is conditional on satisfactory proof of your [[academic and professional qualifications]].
formal.ex_us: The offer is conditional on satisfactory proof of your [[academic and professional credentials]].

everyday.ex: What [[qualifications]] do you need for this job?
everyday.ex_us: What kind of [[degree]] do you need for this job?

collocations: to hold a degree in law
to be educated to master's level
note_fr: « Diploma » désigne en anglais un diplôme précis, souvent court ou professionnel ; le diplôme universitaire est « a degree ». Aux États-Unis, « qualifications » signifie plutôt l'ensemble des aptitudes requises pour le poste ; pour les diplômes, on dit « degrees » ou « credentials ». Et « formation » ne veut jamais dire formation (« training », « education »).

def: A qualification obtained after five years of higher education, equivalent to a master's degree.

formal.ex: Candidates should hold [[a master's degree or equivalent]] (five years of higher education) in human resources or employment law.

everyday.ex: She's got [[a master's]] in employment law from a French university.
everyday.ex_us: She has [[a master's]] in employment law from a French university.

collocations: to be educated to degree level
note_fr: « Bac+5 » ne dit rien à un anglophone : traduisez par le niveau (« master's degree », « bachelor's degree » pour Bac+3) et, si besoin, précisez « five years of higher education ». Aux États-Unis, « graduate degree » = diplôme de deuxième cycle ; au Royaume-Uni, on dit « postgraduate degree ».

explain.written: 'Bac+5' denotes a qualification obtained after five years of higher education following the French baccalauréat, broadly equivalent to a master's degree.
explain.spoken: In France we count the years of study after the school-leaving exam, so 'Bac+5' simply means a master's.

def: The abilities a person has developed and needs in order to do a job well.

formal.ex: The role requires the [[skills and competencies]] listed in the attached specification.

everyday.ex: He's got the technical [[skills]], but I'm less sure about his people management.
everyday.ex_us: He has the technical [[skills]], but I'm less sure about his people management.

informal.ex: She's got years of [[know-how]] in payroll.
informal.ex_us: She has years of [[know-how]] in payroll.

collocations: to have the right skills for the job
note_fr: « Competences » se comprend mais reste du jargon RH (« competency framework » = référentiel de compétences) ; dans la conversation, dites « skills ». « Skill set » désigne l'ensemble des compétences d'une personne. « Capacity » = la capacité de production, pas la compétence.

def: Personal qualities, such as communication and teamwork, that affect how well someone works with others.

formal.ex: Excellent [[interpersonal skills]] and the ability to work under pressure are essential.

everyday.ex: Technically he's brilliant, but the [[soft skills]] need some work.

informal.ex: You need real [[people skills]] to do that job.

note_fr: « Savoir-être » n'a pas d'équivalent mot pour mot : « soft skills » en réunion, « interpersonal skills » dans une annonce. Évitez « know-how-to-be ». Le savoir-faire technique : « hard skills » ou « technical skills ».

def: Everything a person has achieved in their career so far, seen as evidence of what they can do.

formal.ex: The successful candidate will have a [[proven track record]] in managing multi-site HR teams.

everyday.ex: Her [[track record]] in turnaround situations speaks for itself.

collocations: a proven track record in sales
note_fr: « Parcours » se rend selon le sens : « career history » (la chronologie), « career path » (la trajectoire), « background » (la formation et le milieu professionnel), « track record » (les résultats obtenus). « Professional course » serait un contresens : « a course » = un cours.

fr: trou dans le CV / période d'inactivité
def: A period during which a person was not in work, visible in their career history.

formal.ex: Applicants are asked to account for any [[gap in employment]] of more than six months.

everyday.ex: There's a two-year [[gap in her CV]] that nobody asked about.
everyday.ex_us: There's a two-year [[gap in her résumé]] that nobody asked about.

collocations: to take time out to raise a family
note_fr: « A hole in the CV » se comprend mais n'est pas idiomatique. « Career break » est le terme neutre et positif pour une interruption choisie ; on parle aussi de « returners » pour ceux qui reprennent. Interroger sur un « gap » est admis, mais insister sur une maternité ou un état de santé expose à un grief de discrimination.

def: The level of pay a candidate hopes or asks to receive in a new job.

formal.ex: Please indicate your [[salary expectations]] and notice period in your covering letter.
formal.ex_us: Please indicate your [[salary expectations]] and notice period in your cover letter.

everyday.ex: Can I ask [[what you're looking for]] in terms of salary?

collocations: a salary in the region of
note_fr: « Salary pretensions » est un faux ami (« pretension » = prétention, vanité). Attention : dans de nombreux États américains, il est interdit de demander au candidat son salaire actuel ou passé ; interrogez-le sur ses attentes, pas sur son historique.

def: To give false or misleading information about one's degrees, experience or past jobs when applying.

formal.ex: Any candidate found [[to have misrepresented their qualifications]] will be excluded from the selection process.

everyday.ex: Most people [[embellish their CV]] a little, but inventing a degree is another matter.
everyday.ex_us: Most people [[embellish their résumé]] a little, but inventing a degree is another matter.

informal.ex: He'd [[padded his CV]] with a couple of job titles he never held.
informal.ex_us: He'd [[padded his résumé]] with a couple of job titles he never held.

collocations: a false statement on an application
note_fr: « To lie on one's CV » est correct mais abrupt ; « to misrepresent » est le terme des politiques internes et des lettres. En France, un mensonge sur le CV ne justifie pas toujours la rupture : les juges regardent notamment s'il a été déterminant dans l'embauche. Restez donc général et renvoyez à l'avocat.

def: The habit of changing employer frequently, staying only a short time in each job.

formal.ex: The panel noted [[frequent changes of employer]] over the past five years and invited the candidate to comment.

everyday.ex: He's [[moved around a lot]] - four companies in five years.

informal.ex: All that [[job-hopping]] makes me a bit nervous, I must say.
informal.ex_us: All that [[job-hopping]] makes me a little nervous, I have to say.

note_fr: « Job-hopping » est familier et un peu péjoratif : à réserver à l'oral entre collègues. Dans un compte rendu, préférez une formule factuelle (« short tenures », « four employers in five years »). « Instability » évoquerait un trouble psychologique.

def: The first stage of selection, in which applications are read and those that do not meet the requirements are set aside.

formal.ex: The [[initial screening of applications]] is carried out against the essential criteria only.

everyday.ex: I spent the whole afternoon [[sifting CVs]].
everyday.ex_us: I spent the whole afternoon [[screening résumés]].

collocations: to sift through two hundred CVs
note_fr: « To sort CVs » signifie seulement les classer. Pour le tri sélectif : « to screen » (partout) ou « to sift » (UK, littéralement tamiser). « To screen out » = écarter. Si un logiciel ou une IA effectue ce tri, des règles de transparence et de contrôle humain s'appliquent en Europe.

def: To choose, from all the applicants, the small number who will go on to the next stage.

formal.ex: Only [[shortlisted]] candidates will be contacted.
formal.ex_us: Only candidates [[selected for interview]] will be contacted.

everyday.ex: We've [[shortlisted]] four people for interview.
everyday.ex_us: We've [[narrowed it down to]] four people to interview.

collocations: to be shortlisted for a role
note_fr: « Shortlist » (nom et verbe) est omniprésent au Royaume-Uni ; aux États-Unis, il s'emploie aussi, à côté de « finalists » et de « to narrow down the field ». « Preselect » est rare et sonne technique. « To make the shortlist » = figurer parmi les candidats retenus.

def: Software used by employers to collect applications, track candidates through each stage and store their records.

formal.ex: All applications must be logged in the [[applicant tracking system]] within two working days of receipt.
formal.ex_us: All applications must be logged in the [[applicant tracking system]] within two business days of receipt.

everyday.ex: Is she in the [[ATS]] yet? I can't find her record.

collocations: to log an application in the ATS
to move a candidate to the next stage
to run a report from the ATS
note_fr: L'abréviation « ATS » se prononce lettre par lettre. « To log » = enregistrer, saisir. Pour les étapes du processus dans l'outil, on parle de « stages » ou de « pipeline stages », pas de « steps of the tunnel ».

def: A formal meeting at which an employer asks a candidate questions to decide whether to offer them a job.

formal.ex: Each [[selection interview]] shall be conducted by at least two members of staff.

everyday.ex: I've got an [[interview]] with them on Thursday morning.
everyday.ex_us: I have an [[interview]] with them on Thursday morning.

collocations: to have an interview with a company
note_fr: On « has » ou « attends » un entretien ; on ne « passes » pas un entretien pour dire qu'on le passe (« to pass » = réussir). « Hiring interview » est rare. Notez l'emploi britannique sans article : « at interview », « to be invited to interview ».

fr: faire passer un entretien à quelqu'un
def: To meet a candidate and ask them questions in order to assess them for a job.

formal.ex: Managers must complete the training module before [[conducting an interview]].

everyday.ex: We're [[interviewing]] three people on Monday.

informal.ex: I'm [[seeing]] two more candidates this afternoon.

collocations: to interview someone for a role
to sit in on an interview
note_fr: Le verbe est transitif direct : « to interview a candidate ». « To make pass an interview » est impossible. « To sit in on an interview » = y assister en observateur. « Interviewer » = celui qui mène l'entretien ; « interviewee » = le candidat.

term.us: to invite someone for an interview

def: To ask a candidate to come to a meeting where they will be assessed for the job.

formal.uk: to invite to attend an interview
formal.us: to invite to attend an interview
formal.ex: We are pleased [[to invite you to attend an interview]] at our offices on Tuesday 3 June at 10 a.m.
formal.ex_us: We are pleased [[to invite you to attend an interview]] at our offices on Tuesday, June 3, at 10 a.m.

everyday.uk: to get someone in for an interview
everyday.us: to bring someone in for an interview
everyday.ex: Let's [[get her in for an interview]] next week.
everyday.ex_us: Let's [[bring her in for an interview]] next week.

note_fr: « To convoke » est archaïque, et « to summon » (sommer de comparaître) ferait fuir le candidat : en anglais, on « invite ». Réservez « to call someone to a meeting » aux réunions disciplinaires. Fixer un entretien : « to schedule » ou « to arrange an interview ».

def: A short first conversation by phone to check a candidate's basic suitability before a full interview.

formal.ex: Shortlisted candidates will first be invited to a [[preliminary telephone interview]] lasting approximately thirty minutes.

everyday.ex: I did a quick [[phone interview]] with him yesterday and he came across well.
everyday.ex_us: I did a quick [[phone screen]] with him yesterday and he came across well.

informal.ex: Let's have [[a quick call]] with her before we bring her in.

note_fr: « Phone screen » (nom) et « to phone-screen » (verbe) sont typiquement américains. « To come across well » = faire bonne impression. L'entretien en visioconférence : « a video interview » ; s'il est préenregistré, sans interlocuteur, « a one-way video interview ».

def: An interview in which every candidate is asked the same prepared questions and scored in the same way.

formal.ex: A [[structured interview]], based on a common set of questions, shall be used for all shortlisted candidates.

everyday.uk: to ask everyone the same questions
everyday.us: to ask everyone the same questions
everyday.ex: It's fairer if we [[ask everyone the same questions]] and score them as we go.

collocations: to score answers against the criteria
note_fr: L'entretien structuré est la meilleure protection contre un grief de discrimination : mêmes questions, même grille, notes conservées. « Interview guide » = trame d'entretien. « To probe » = creuser une réponse par des questions de relance (« follow-up questions »).

fr: entretien comportemental (fondé sur des situations vécues)
def: An interview in which candidates are asked to describe real past situations as evidence of specific skills.

formal.ex: The second stage consists of a [[competency-based interview]] with two senior managers.
formal.ex_us: The second stage consists of a [[behavioral interview]] with two senior managers.

everyday.ex: Prepare some examples - they always ask [[competency questions]].
everyday.ex_us: Prepare some examples - they always ask [[behavioral questions]].

collocations: Tell me about a time when...
Can you give me an example of...
note_fr: La question type commence par « Tell me about a time when... » et appelle une réponse structurée selon la méthode STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result). Orthographe : « behavioural » (UK), « behavioral » (US). À distinguer de la « situational question », hypothétique : « What would you do if... ? »

def: The group of people who interview a candidate together and assess them.

formal.ex: The [[selection panel]] shall include at least one member who has completed recruitment training.

everyday.ex: Who's on the [[interview panel]] for the finance role?

note_fr: « Jury » est réservé aux procès et aux concours : pour un recrutement, on dit « panel ». « To sit on a panel » = en faire partie ; « to chair the panel » = le présider. Un entretien devant plusieurs personnes est « a panel interview ».

term.uk: to progress to the next stage
term.us: to move on to the next round

ipa.us: /tə ˌmuːv ˈɑːn tə ðə ˌnekst ˈraʊnd/

def: To be selected to continue in a recruitment process after an interview or test.

formal.uk: to progress to the next stage
formal.us: to advance to the next stage
formal.ex: We are pleased to inform you that you [[have progressed to the next stage]] of the selection process.
formal.ex_us: We are pleased to inform you that you [[have advanced to the next stage]] of the selection process.

everyday.uk: to get through to the next round
everyday.us: to move on to the next round
everyday.ex: Only two of them [[got through to the next round]].
everyday.ex_us: Only two of them [[moved on to the next round]].

note_fr: Côté employeur, la tournure élégante est « We'd like to take your application forward ». « To pass to the next step » est un calque. « Round » (tour) est fréquent aux États-Unis ; « stage » domine au Royaume-Uni.

def: The things a person does well and the things they do less well.

formal.ex: The report summarises each candidate's [[strengths and areas for development]].

everyday.ex: What would you say are your main [[strengths and weaknesses]]?

note_fr: « Strong points » et « weak points » se comprennent, mais « strengths » et « weaknesses » sont plus naturels. Dans un compte rendu, l'euphémisme d'usage pour les faiblesses est « areas for development » ou « development needs ». « Défaut » ne se dit jamais « default ».

def: A selection test in which the candidate carries out a task that closely resembles the real work.

formal.ex: Candidates will complete a [[job simulation exercise]] designed to reflect the daily demands of the role.

everyday.ex: We give them a [[practical exercise]] - drafting a reply to a difficult employee email.

note_fr: « Situation setting » n'existe pas. Selon l'exercice : « role play » (jeu de rôle), « case study » (étude de cas), « in-tray exercise » (UK) ou « in-basket exercise » (US) pour le traitement d'une corbeille de courrier, « presentation exercise ».

def: A selection event, often lasting a day, where a group of candidates take part in tests, exercises and interviews observed by assessors.

formal.ex: Candidates who pass the online tests will be invited to attend an [[assessment centre]] in Manchester.
formal.ex_us: Candidates who pass the online tests will be invited to attend an [[assessment center]] in Chicago.

everyday.ex: The [[assessment day]] is tough: a group exercise, a presentation and two interviews.

note_fr: Faux lieu : un « assessment centre » n'est pas un bâtiment mais une méthode, une journée d'épreuves. On y « attend » (on y participe). Les évaluateurs sont des « assessors ». Très utilisé au Royaume-Uni pour les jeunes diplômés ; moins répandu sous ce nom aux États-Unis.

def: Standardised tests used in selection to measure a candidate's reasoning ability or personality.

formal.ex: [[Psychometric testing]] forms part of the selection process for all management positions.
formal.ex_us: [[Pre-employment testing]] forms part of the selection process for all management positions.

everyday.ex: They made me sit two [[psychometric tests]] before I'd even met anyone.
everyday.ex_us: They made me take two [[assessments]] before I'd even met anyone.

collocations: to sit a test (UK) / to take a test (US)
note_fr: « Psychotechnical » ne se dit pas. Un Britannique « sits » ou « takes » a test ; un Américain « takes » a test ; personne ne « passes » un test, sauf pour dire qu'il l'a réussi. En droit français, les méthodes d'évaluation doivent être pertinentes au regard du poste et le candidat doit en être informé au préalable.

def: A table used to give each candidate a mark against each selection criterion.

formal.ex: Each panel member shall complete a [[scoring matrix]] independently before any discussion takes place.
formal.ex_us: Each panel member shall complete a [[scorecard]] independently before any discussion takes place.

everyday.ex: Fill in your [[score sheet]] before we compare notes, please.
everyday.ex_us: Fill in your [[scorecard]] before we compare notes, please.

collocations: to score a candidate against the criteria
note_fr: « Evaluation grid » se comprend mais sent la traduction. « To score against the criteria » = noter au regard des critères ; « to weight » = pondérer. Ces grilles sont à conserver : ce sont elles qui permettent de justifier la décision en cas de contestation.

def: How well a candidate's skills, values and way of working match the job and the organisation.

formal.ex: The interview is designed to assess the candidate's [[suitability for the role]] against objective criteria.

everyday.ex: On paper she's [[a good fit]], but I'd like a second opinion.

informal.ex: Nice guy, but he's just not [[the right fit]] for us.

collocations: to be a good fit for the role
note_fr: « Adequacy » signifie « caractère suffisant » : contresens. « Fit » est pratique mais dangereux : « cultural fit » sert trop souvent à écarter ceux qui ne ressemblent pas à l'équipe. Dans un écrit, rattachez toujours la décision à des critères objectifs (« suitability », « meets the criteria »).

def: A short practical test in which a candidate does real tasks so the employer can judge their ability before deciding to hire.

formal.ex: Any [[work trial]] must be brief, strictly limited to assessing the candidate's skills and agreed in advance.
formal.ex_us: Any [[working interview]] must be brief, strictly limited to assessing the candidate's skills and agreed in advance.

everyday.ex: We asked him to do a [[trial shift]] in the kitchen on Saturday.
everyday.ex_us: We asked him to do a [[working interview]] in the kitchen on Saturday.

collocations: to be paid for one's time
note_fr: Ne confondez pas avec la période d'essai (« probationary period »), qui suppose un contrat déjà conclu. En France, l'essai professionnel doit rester un test bref, hors conditions normales d'emploi ; s'il se prolonge ou devient productif, il risque d'être analysé comme un contrat de travail. Aux États-Unis et au Royaume-Uni, un essai qui profite à l'entreprise doit en principe être payé.

def: To check a candidate's background and claims carefully before deciding to appoint them.

formal.uk: to carry out due diligence on
formal.us: to carry out due diligence on
formal.ex: The firm will [[carry out due diligence on]] the preferred candidate before an offer is confirmed.

everyday.ex: The agency is supposed [[to vet]] everyone before they send them over.

note_fr: « To vet » n'a rien de vétérinaire ici : c'est contrôler soigneusement. « Vetting » désigne en particulier, au Royaume-Uni, l'habilitation de sécurité. Toute vérification doit rester proportionnée au poste, et le candidat doit en être informé.

def: The person who is chosen for the job at the end of the selection process.

formal.ex: The [[successful candidate]] will report to the Head of Human Resources.

everyday.ex: [[The person we've chosen]] can't start until September.
everyday.ex_us: [[The person we chose]] can't start until September.

collocations: to be appointed to a post
note_fr: « The retained candidate » est un calque (« to retain » = fidéliser, garder un salarié). On dit « the successful candidate » et, pour les autres, « unsuccessful candidates ». Tant que l'offre n'est pas acceptée, on parle du « preferred candidate ».

def: To decide not to take a candidate any further and to tell them so.

formal.ex: We regret to inform you that on this occasion your application [[has been unsuccessful]].

everyday.ex: We had [[to turn him down]] - he just didn't have the experience.

collocations: to let a candidate down gently
not to take an application any further
note_fr: Dans une lettre, on évite « rejected » et « refused » : la formule consacrée est « your application has been unsuccessful » ou « we will not be taking your application any further ». « On this occasion » adoucit et laisse la porte ouverte. « To let someone down gently » = annoncer un refus avec tact.

def: To contact someone again later with an answer or a decision.

formal.ex: We will [[revert to you]] once the panel has reached its decision.
formal.ex_us: We will [[respond to you]] once the panel has reached its decision.

everyday.ex: I'll [[get back to you]] by Friday at the latest.

collocations: to get back to someone by Friday
to let someone know either way
note_fr: « I come back to you » est le calque le plus répandu chez les francophones. Dites « I'll get back to you » ou « I'll be in touch ». « To revert to » dans ce sens est admis dans les e-mails formels britanniques, mais critiqué et rare aux États-Unis, où « revert » signifie seulement « revenir à un état antérieur ».

def: To tell an employer that one no longer wishes to be considered for a job.

formal.ex: I regret to inform you that I have decided [[to withdraw my application]] for the position of Compliance Officer.

everyday.ex: Our first choice [[pulled out]] at the last minute.
everyday.ex_us: Our first choice [[dropped out]] at the last minute.

informal.ex: He seemed keen, then he just [[ghosted]] us.

collocations: to pull out of the process
to drop out at the final stage
note_fr: « To desist » = cesser (un comportement), jamais « se désister ». « To ghost » (cesser de répondre sans explication) vient du vocabulaire amoureux et reste familier ; il s'emploie dans les deux sens, car les employeurs aussi « ghost » les candidats.

fr: candidat de réserve (second choix en cas de désistement)
def: A candidate who was not chosen but would be offered the job if the first choice declined.

formal.ex: The panel also identified a [[reserve candidate]], to whom the post will be offered should the first candidate decline.
formal.ex_us: The panel also identified an [[alternate candidate]], to whom the position will be offered should the first candidate decline.

everyday.ex: Don't turn anyone down yet - we need to keep our [[second choice]] warm.
everyday.ex_us: Don't turn anyone down yet - we need to keep our [[backup candidate]] warm.

collocations: to hold a candidate in reserve
note_fr: « To keep a candidate warm » = entretenir l'intérêt d'un candidat sans rien lui promettre. Par prudence, n'envoyez pas les réponses négatives avant que le premier choix ait accepté. « The offer fell through » = l'offre n'a pas abouti.

fr: égalité des chances (dans l'accès à l'emploi)
def: The principle that everyone should have the same chance of being hired, whatever their sex, origin, age or other personal characteristics.

formal.ex: The Company is committed to [[equal opportunities]] at every stage of recruitment and selection.
formal.ex_us: The Company is committed to [[equal employment opportunity]] at every stage of recruitment and selection.

everyday.ex: Same questions for everybody - we want [[a level playing field]].

note_fr: « Equality of chances » est un calque (« chance » = hasard). Au Royaume-Uni : « equal opportunities » (pluriel) ; aux États-Unis : « equal employment opportunity » (EEO), d'où la mention « We are an equal opportunity employer » au bas des annonces. Les critères protégés ne sont pas identiques dans les trois pays.

def: An unfair preference or prejudice that influences a decision without the person being aware of it.

formal.ex: All members of selection panels are required to complete [[unconscious bias]] training.
formal.ex_us: All members of selection panels are required to complete [[implicit bias]] training.

everyday.ex: We can't turn someone down on a [[gut feeling]] - what does the score sheet say?
everyday.ex_us: We can't turn someone down on a [[gut feeling]] - what does the scorecard say?

note_fr: « Bias » est indénombrable ou dénombrable, et l'adjectif est « biased » : « he is biased », jamais « he is bias ». On est « biased against » (défavorablement) ou « in favour of » (US : « in favor of »). « Implicit bias » est plus courant aux États-Unis.

def: A way of selecting in which names and other personal details are removed from applications so that they cannot influence the decision.

formal.ex: Shortlisting shall be carried out on the basis of [[anonymised applications]].
formal.ex_us: Screening shall be carried out on the basis of [[anonymized applications]].

everyday.ex: We've moved to [[name-blind CVs]] for the first sift.
everyday.ex_us: We've moved to [[blind résumés]] for the first screen.

note_fr: « Anonymous CV » laisserait croire que le candidat a lui-même caché son identité : dites « anonymised » (UK) / « anonymized » (US) ou « blind ». « To redact » = occulter une mention dans un document. En France comme au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, la pratique reste volontaire.

def: Questions an interviewer should not ask because they touch on personal matters unrelated to the job and may lead to discrimination.

formal.uk: questions unrelated to the requirements of the role
formal.us: questions unrelated to the requirements of the position
formal.ex: Interviewers must refrain from asking [[questions unrelated to the requirements of the role]], in particular about family circumstances or health.
formal.ex_us: Interviewers must refrain from asking [[questions unrelated to the requirements of the position]], in particular about family circumstances or health.

everyday.ex: Anything about children or plans to start a family is strictly [[off-limits]].

collocations: to steer clear of personal questions
to be none of the employer's business
note_fr: En droit français, les informations demandées à un candidat ne peuvent servir qu'à apprécier sa capacité à occuper l'emploi et doivent avoir un lien direct et nécessaire avec celui-ci. L'esprit est le même au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, mais par le biais du droit de la discrimination : une question sur l'âge, la famille ou la santé servira de preuve contre l'employeur. « Forbidden questions » sonne enfantin.

def: A narrow legal exception allowing an employer to require a particular characteristic, such as sex, where the nature of the job genuinely demands it.

formal.ex: The advertisement may specify a female candidate only where this constitutes a [[genuine occupational requirement]].
formal.ex_us: The advertisement may specify a female candidate only where this constitutes a [[bona fide occupational qualification]].

everyday.uk: a genuine requirement of the job
everyday.ex: You can only ask for a woman if it's [[a genuine requirement of the job]] - and that's rare.
everyday.ex_us: You can only ask for a woman if it's [[a BFOQ]] - and that's rare.

collocations: to rely on an occupational requirement
a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim
to be justified by the nature of the work
note_fr: Trois noms pour une même exception, toujours interprétée strictement : « exigence professionnelle essentielle et déterminante » en France, « occupational requirement » au Royaume-Uni, « bona fide occupational qualification » (BFOQ) aux États-Unis, où elle ne peut jamais porter sur la race. Dans le doute, n'inscrivez aucun critère personnel dans une annonce.

def: A final group of candidates that includes people from different backgrounds, not all of the same sex or origin.

formal.ex: Search firms are asked to present a [[diverse shortlist]] for every senior appointment.
formal.ex_us: Search firms are asked to present a [[diverse slate of candidates]] for every senior appointment.

everyday.ex: The agency sent us five men again - I've asked them for a [[balanced shortlist]].
everyday.ex_us: The agency sent us five men again - I've asked them for a [[diverse slate]].

collocations: to widen the pool of applicants
note_fr: Élargir le vivier est licite partout ; choisir un candidat en raison de son sexe ou de son origine ne l'est généralement pas. Vocabulaire : « positive action » (UK) désigne des mesures d'encouragement encadrées, « positive discrimination » y est illicite ; « affirmative action » est le terme américain, aujourd'hui très contesté. Ne promettez jamais de « quotas » à la légère.

def: Statements from former employers or other people confirming a candidate's past work and character.

formal.ex: References will only be [[taken up]] once a conditional offer has been made.
formal.ex_us: References will only be [[checked]] once a conditional offer has been made.

everyday.ex: Have we [[followed up her references]] yet?
everyday.ex_us: Have we [[checked her references]] yet?

note_fr: On ne « takes » pas des références au sens français : au Royaume-Uni, on les « takes up » ou « follows up » ; aux États-Unis, on les « checks ». En France, l'employeur ne contacte un ancien employeur qu'après en avoir informé le candidat. Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, beaucoup d'entreprises ne confirment que les dates et l'intitulé du poste.

def: A person, usually a former manager, who agrees to confirm a candidate's experience and character to a new employer.

formal.ex: Please give the names and contact details of two [[referees]], one of whom should be your current employer.
formal.ex_us: Please give the names and contact details of two [[references]], one of whom should be your current employer.

everyday.ex: My old boss has agreed [[to act as a referee]].
everyday.ex_us: My old boss has agreed [[to be a reference]].

collocations: to name someone as a referee
to list someone as a reference
note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, la personne est « a referee » et son témoignage « a reference » ; aux États-Unis, « reference » désigne les deux, et « referee » n'évoque que l'arbitre sportif. « To vouch for someone » = se porter garant de quelqu'un. Ne confondez pas avec « referral » (cooptation, recommandation).

def: A check of whether a candidate has criminal convictions, carried out where the nature of the job justifies it.

formal.ex: Given the nature of the role, the offer is subject to a satisfactory [[criminal record check]].
formal.ex_us: Given the nature of the role, the offer is subject to a satisfactory [[criminal background check]].

everyday.ex: You can't work with children until your [[DBS check]] has come through.
everyday.ex_us: You can't work with children until your [[background check]] has come through.

note_fr: « Judicial case » ne veut rien dire : le casier est « a criminal record ». En France, l'employeur ne peut demander un extrait (bulletin n° 3) que si le poste le justifie, et c'est le candidat qui le fournit. Au Royaume-Uni, le contrôle passe par le Disclosure and Barring Service (« DBS check »). Aux États-Unis, il exige le consentement écrit du candidat, et de nombreux États et villes interdisent de poser la question avant un certain stade (lois dites « ban the box »).

def: Confirmation, obtained from the school or university, that a candidate really holds the degrees they claim.

formal.ex: The offer is conditional upon [[verification of academic qualifications]] by a third-party provider.
formal.ex_us: The offer is conditional upon [[verification of academic credentials]] by a third-party provider.

everyday.ex: Did anyone actually [[check his degree]]? I can't find the certificate on file.

note_fr: L'original du diplôme est « a degree certificate » (UK) ou « a diploma » (US, le parchemin lui-même) ; le relevé de notes, « a transcript ». Une copie certifiée conforme : « a certified copy ». Prévenez le candidat que la vérification aura lieu et obtenez son accord.

def: An official document allowing a foreign national to live in a country for a given period.

formal.ex: The Employee shall inform the Company without delay of any change affecting the validity of his or her [[residence permit]].

everyday.ex: Her [[residence permit]] runs out in March, so she needs to renew it soon.

informal.ex: He's still waiting for his [[papers]] to come through.

collocations: to hold a valid residence permit
note_fr: « Title of stay » est un calque. Les équivalents fonctionnels : « visa » ou « leave to remain » au Royaume-Uni (preuve désormais numérique, « eVisa »), « green card » aux États-Unis pour le résident permanent. Tous les titres de séjour français n'autorisent pas à travailler : vérifiez la mention portée sur le document.

def: Official permission for a foreign national to take up employment in a country.

formal.ex: The employer must apply for [[authorisation to work]] before the foreign national takes up the post.
formal.ex_us: The employer must apply for [[employment authorization]] before the foreign national takes up the position.

everyday.ex: Does he need a [[work permit]], or can he start straight away?
everyday.ex_us: Does he need [[work authorization]], or can he start right away?

collocations: to apply for a work permit
to be authorised to work in France
to be granted a work permit
note_fr: En France, l'employeur qui recrute un étranger doit s'assurer, avant l'embauche, qu'il détient un titre l'autorisant à travailler et en faire vérifier l'authenticité auprès de la préfecture ; employer un étranger sans titre est une infraction pénale. Au Royaume-Uni, on parle de « right to work » ; aux États-Unis, de « work authorization », vérifiée au moyen du formulaire I-9.

fr: parrainer un salarié étranger (prendre en charge sa demande de visa de travail)
def: To act as the employer officially supporting a foreign national's application for a work visa.

formal.ex: The Company is licensed [[to sponsor]] skilled workers from outside the United Kingdom.
formal.ex_us: The Company is willing [[to sponsor]] qualified foreign nationals for employment-based visas.

everyday.ex: Would you be willing [[to sponsor my visa]]?

note_fr: Rien à voir avec le mécénat sportif. Au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur doit détenir une « sponsor licence » ; aux États-Unis, il « sponsors » le visa (H-1B, par exemple) ou la carte verte. La question type des annonces américaines : « Will you now or in the future require sponsorship? » En France, on parle plutôt de demande d'autorisation de travail déposée par l'employeur.

def: A person who is not a citizen of the country, or group of countries, in which they wish to work.

formal.ex: A [[third-country national]] may be employed only if he or she holds a document authorising him or her to work in France.
formal.ex_us: A [[foreign national]] may be employed only if he or she holds a document authorizing him or her to work in the United States.

everyday.ex: Hiring [[someone from outside the EU]] takes a couple of months longer, so plan ahead.
everyday.ex_us: Hiring [[someone from overseas]] takes a couple of months longer, so plan ahead.

note_fr: « Third-country national » est le terme du droit européen, incompris hors de ce contexte : expliquez-le à un Américain. « Ressortissant » se dit « national » ou « citizen », jamais « resortissant ». Évitez « alien », encore présent dans les textes américains mais ressenti comme blessant, et « foreigner », peu aimable.

fr: faire une offre à un candidat
def: To tell a candidate formally that the employer wants to hire them, and on what terms.

formal.uk: to make an offer of employment
formal.us: to extend an offer of employment
formal.ex: The Company intends [[to make an offer of employment]] to the preferred candidate this week.
formal.ex_us: The Company intends [[to extend an offer of employment]] to the preferred candidate this week.

everyday.ex: We'd like [[to make you an offer]].

informal.ex: They rang this morning and [[offered me the job]]!
informal.ex_us: They called this morning and [[offered me the job]]!

collocations: to put an offer in writing
note_fr: On « makes » une offre ; « to extend an offer » est le tour formel américain. « To do an offer » et « to propose a job to someone » sont des calques. N'oubliez pas qu'en France une offre ferme et précise engage l'employeur : faites valider les termes avant de les annoncer, même oralement.

def: A new offer made in reply to one that was not accepted as it stood - by the candidate, or by the current employer to stop them leaving.

formal.ex: The candidate has made a [[counter-offer]] in respect of the basic salary and the start date.
formal.ex_us: The candidate has made a [[counteroffer]] with respect to the base salary and the start date.

everyday.ex: She [[came back with]] a request for five thousand more and an extra day at home.

note_fr: Deux sens à distinguer : la contre-proposition du candidat, et la surenchère de son employeur actuel pour le retenir (« his current employer made him a counter-offer »). « To match an offer » = s'aligner. « There's some room for manoeuvre » (US : « some wiggle room ») = il y a une marge de négociation.

fr: aide à la mobilité (prise en charge du déménagement)
def: The financial and practical help an employer offers a new recruit who has to move home to take the job.

formal.ex: The Company will provide [[relocation assistance]] up to the amount set out in the offer letter, against receipts.

everyday.ex: Is there a [[relocation package]]? I'd be moving my whole family from Lisbon.

note_fr: « Delocalisation » désigne le transfert d'une activité à l'étranger, pas le déménagement d'un salarié : pour une personne, on dit « to relocate ». « Removal costs » (UK) = « moving expenses » (US). « Against receipts » = sur justificatifs.

def: The declaration a French employer must file with the social security authorities before a new employee starts work.

formal.ex: The employer must file the [[pre-hiring declaration]] (DPAE) with URSSAF before the employee takes up his or her duties.

everyday.ex: Don't let him start on Monday until we've [[registered him]] with the social security office.

collocations: to register a new employee with the authorities
to be filed before the start date
note_fr: Aucun équivalent exact. Au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur déclare le nouveau salarié à l'administration fiscale via la paie ; aux États-Unis, il existe un « new hire reporting » auprès de l'État, mais après l'embauche. Insistez sur le « before » : l'absence de DPAE expose à des sanctions pour travail dissimulé (« undeclared work »).

explain.written: The DPAE (déclaration préalable à l'embauche) is a mandatory declaration which the employer must file with the social security collection body (URSSAF) before a new employee starts work.
explain.spoken: Before anyone starts, we have to register them online with the French social security office - it only takes a few minutes, but it has to be done before day one.

def: The record a French employer must keep, listing everyone hired in the order in which they joined.

formal.ex: The new employee's details must be entered in the [[statutory staff register]] at the time of hiring.

everyday.ex: Have we added the two interns to the [[staff register]]?

collocations: to enter someone in the staff register
to keep the register up to date
to produce the register on request
note_fr: Il n'existe pas de registre équivalent au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis, où l'on parle simplement de « personnel records ». En France, il est tenu par établissement, dans l'ordre des embauches, et les stagiaires y figurent dans une partie distincte. L'inspecteur du travail peut le demander : « a labour inspector » (US : « labor »).

explain.written: The registre unique du personnel is a mandatory register in which a French employer records, in chronological order of hiring, every employee of the establishment, with a separate section for interns.
explain.spoken: It's a register French companies have to keep - everyone we take on goes in it, in order of arrival, and the labour inspector can ask to see it.

fr: visite d'information et de prévention (ex-visite médicale d'embauche)
def: The appointment with the occupational health service that every new employee in France must have shortly after joining.

formal.ex: The Employee shall attend an [[initial occupational health appointment]] arranged by the Company after joining.

everyday.ex: HR will book your [[occupational health check]] in your first few weeks.

collocations: to book an appointment with occupational health
to be declared fit for work
note_fr: Ce n'est plus, sauf pour les postes à risques, une visite d'aptitude préalable : c'est un rendez-vous d'information organisé après la prise de poste par le service de prévention et de santé au travail. Au Royaume-Uni, un questionnaire de santé ne peut en principe être demandé qu'après l'offre ; aux États-Unis, un examen médical n'est possible qu'après une offre conditionnelle. « Work doctor » ne se dit pas : « occupational health physician ».

explain.written: The visite d'information et de prévention is a mandatory appointment with the occupational health service, which every new employee must attend shortly after starting work; employees in high-risk jobs undergo a medical fitness examination instead.
explain.spoken: In France every new joiner has an appointment with occupational health in their first few months - it's not a fitness test, more of an information session, and the company arranges it.

def: A fixed period spent working in a company as part of a course of study, in order to gain practical experience.

formal.ex: Students are required to complete a [[work placement]] of at least three months during their final year.
formal.ex_us: Students are required to complete an [[internship]] of at least three months during their final year.

everyday.ex: She did a six-month [[internship]] with us before we took her on.

collocations: to take an intern on permanently
note_fr: Faux ami célèbre : « a stage » est une scène ou une étape, « a training course » une formation. Dites « internship » (partout) ou « work placement » (UK, surtout dans le cadre d'un cursus). On « does » un stage, on ne le « makes » pas.

def: A student or recent graduate who works in a company for a limited period to gain experience.

formal.ex: A [[student on placement]] is not an employee and must not be assigned to a permanent post.
formal.ex_us: An [[intern]] is not an employee and must not be assigned to a permanent position.

everyday.ex: We've got two [[interns]] joining the team in June.
everyday.ex_us: We have two [[interns]] joining the team in June.

note_fr: « Trainee » n'est pas un stagiaire : c'est un salarié débutant en formation (« a trainee solicitor », « a management trainee »). « Stagiaire » n'est compris que dans les cuisines et les institutions européennes. En France, le stagiaire n'est pas salarié ; aux États-Unis et au Royaume-Uni, un « intern » qui effectue un vrai travail a en principe droit au salaire minimum.

def: The three-party agreement, compulsory in France, signed by the student, the host company and the school before an internship begins.

formal.ex: No intern may begin work until the [[tripartite internship agreement]] has been signed by the student, the educational institution and the host organisation.
formal.ex_us: No intern may begin work until the [[tripartite internship agreement]] has been signed by the student, the educational institution and the host organization.

everyday.ex: We can't let her start without a signed [[internship agreement]] from her school.

note_fr: « Convention » seul est un faux ami (congrès, usage). L'accord est tripartite, et c'est ce qui le distingue : sans établissement d'enseignement, pas de stage en France. Le stage ne peut pas servir à pourvoir un poste permanent ni à remplacer un salarié absent. Rien de comparable n'est exigé par la loi au Royaume-Uni ou aux États-Unis.

explain.written: A convention de stage is the mandatory three-party agreement between the student, the educational institution and the host organisation which governs an internship in France; the intern is not an employee.
explain.spoken: In France you can't just take on an intern - there has to be a three-way agreement signed with the student's school, and the intern isn't an employee.

def: The minimum monthly payment a French host organisation must make to an intern once the internship exceeds a certain length.

formal.ex: The intern shall receive a monthly [[internship allowance]] at the rate provided for by law.
formal.ex_us: The intern shall receive a monthly [[internship stipend]] at the rate provided for by law.

everyday.ex: It isn't a salary - [[what interns get paid]] is a fixed monthly allowance.

collocations: to pay an intern an allowance
to be exempt from social security contributions
note_fr: « Gratification » en anglais signifie satisfaction, plaisir : faux ami complet. Ce n'est pas non plus un « salary » ni un « wage », puisque le stagiaire n'est pas salarié : dites « allowance » (UK) ou « stipend » (US). Elle devient obligatoire au-delà d'une durée minimale de stage fixée par la loi, et son montant plancher est réglementé.

explain.written: The gratification de stage is the minimum monthly allowance which the host organisation must pay an intern whose internship exceeds the length laid down by law; it is not a salary.
explain.spoken: Interns in France aren't paid a salary, but once the internship goes beyond a certain length the company has to pay them a set monthly allowance.

def: The process of helping a new employee settle in, learn how the organisation works and become effective.

formal.ex: The [[onboarding process]] begins when the offer is accepted and continues throughout the first six months.

everyday.ex: How's the new analyst [[settling in]]?

note_fr: « Integration » évoque en anglais l'intégration des minorités ou des systèmes informatiques, pas l'accueil d'un salarié. « Onboarding » s'est imposé partout, y compris comme verbe (« to onboard someone »). « To settle in » = prendre ses marques.

def: The introduction given to new employees in their first days: the organisation, its rules, the people and the premises.

formal.ex: All new employees are required to attend the [[induction programme]] during their first week.
formal.ex_us: All new employees are required to attend [[new hire orientation]] during their first week.

everyday.ex: Your [[induction]] is on Monday morning - HR will show you round.
everyday.ex_us: Your [[orientation]] is on Monday morning - HR will show you around.

note_fr: « Induction » est britannique ; un Américain dira « orientation ». « Welcome day » se comprend mais n'est pas le terme consacré. Le livret d'accueil remis ce jour-là : « a welcome pack » (UK), « a welcome packet / kit » (US).

def: A person who has just joined an organisation.

formal.ex: Each [[new employee]] shall be given a copy of the internal rules on his or her first day.

everyday.ex: We've got three [[new starters]] next week, so the desks need sorting out.
everyday.ex_us: We've got three [[new hires]] next week, so the desks need to be set up.

informal.ex: I'm still the [[newbie]] here - I only started in March.

note_fr: « New starter » et « new joiner » sont britanniques, « new hire » américain mais compris partout ; « new recruit » est neutre. « Newcomer » désigne plutôt un nouvel arrivant dans une ville ou un secteur. « Newbie » est familier et affectueux.

def: A colleague chosen to help a new employee informally during their first weeks.

formal.ex: Each new starter is assigned a [[workplace buddy]] for the first three months.
formal.ex_us: Each new hire is assigned an [[onboarding buddy]] for the first three months.

everyday.ex: Priya will be your [[buddy]], so just ask her if you get stuck.

collocations: to take someone under one's wing
note_fr: « Godfather » évoque la mafia et « sponsor » un appui de carrière au plus haut niveau : pour l'accueil au quotidien, le mot est « buddy », parfaitement admis en contexte professionnel. « Mentor » désigne un accompagnement plus durable. « To show someone the ropes » = montrer les ficelles du métier.

def: To reach the level of knowledge needed to do a new job properly.

formal.uk: to become fully effective in the role
formal.us: to become fully effective in the role
formal.ex: The induction plan is designed to enable the new manager [[to become fully effective in the role]] within three months.

everyday.ex: Give her a few weeks [[to get up to speed]] before you judge.

informal.ex: It took me a good month [[to find my feet]].

collocations: to bring someone up to speed
note_fr: « Operational » s'applique aux machines et aux services, rarement aux personnes : « she is operational » fait sourire. Dites « up to speed » ou « fully effective ». « To hit the ground running » = être efficace dès le premier jour ; « a steep learning curve » = un apprentissage exigeant (et non facile).

def: A short report in which a new employee sets out what has surprised them about the organisation during their first weeks.

formal.ex: After two months, each new manager is invited to submit a [[first-impressions report]] to the HR Director.

everyday.ex: You're [[a fresh pair of eyes]], so tell us what struck you - good and bad.

collocations: to take a fresh look at something
to see something with fresh eyes
note_fr: « Astonishment report » ferait sourire : la pratique est très française et n'a pas de nom établi en anglais. Glosez-la, ou rapprochez-la de ce que les anglophones connaissent : « new joiner survey », « 90-day feedback ». L'idée se dit très bien avec « a fresh pair of eyes ».

explain.written: A rapport d'étonnement is a short report, common in French companies, in which a new recruit records his or her first impressions of the organisation - what works well and what seems surprising - after a few weeks in post.
explain.spoken: It's a French habit: after a few weeks we ask new joiners to write down what surprised them, because they see things the rest of us no longer notice.

fr: pré-intégration (entre l'acceptation de l'offre et l'arrivée)
def: Everything an employer does to prepare and stay in touch with a new recruit between the acceptance of the offer and the first day.

formal.ex: The [[pre-joining arrangements]] include the issue of IT equipment and access to the staff intranet.
formal.ex_us: The [[pre-start arrangements]] include the issue of IT equipment and access to the employee intranet.

everyday.ex: Good [[preboarding]] is the best way to stop people changing their minds during their notice period.

collocations: to keep in touch before day one
note_fr: Le risque pendant cette période s'appelle familièrement « a no-show » : le candidat qui ne se présente pas le premier jour. « To get someone set up » = préparer son matériel et ses accès. « To have second thoughts » = se raviser.

def: The number of days between the start of a recruitment process and the candidate's acceptance of the offer.

formal.ex: Average [[time to hire]] fell from fifty-two to forty-one days over the reporting period.

everyday.uk: how long it takes to hire
everyday.us: how long it takes to hire
everyday.ex: Honestly, [[how long it takes us to hire]] is what loses us the best people.

note_fr: Deux indicateurs voisins : « time to fill » court de l'ouverture du poste à l'acceptation de l'offre ; « time to hire », de l'entrée du candidat dans le processus à son acceptation. « Delay » est un faux ami : c'est un retard, pas un délai.

def: The total amount spent on recruitment divided by the number of people hired.

formal.ex: [[Cost per hire]] includes agency fees, advertising and the time spent by internal staff.

everyday.ex: Once you add the agency fee, [[what each hire costs us]] is frightening.

collocations: to bring down the cost per hire
note_fr: « Hire » est aussi un nom : « a hire » = une embauche ou la personne embauchée (« a good hire », « a bad hire »). Les honoraires de cabinet se disent « placement fee » ou « agency fee », généralement un pourcentage du salaire annuel.
